questions.q: What is use-case development, and why does it start from a risk rather than a rule catalog?
options: A scheduling process for when analysts take shifts
A method for deleting all out-of-the-box rules without replacement
A process for renaming existing SIEM rules to match company branding
Building detection logic starting from a specific real risk the organization cares about, rather than simply enabling generic pre-built rules
questions.explain: Use-case development starts from a named, real risk and builds or tunes the exact logic needed to catch it.

questions.q: In the lateral movement example, why do authentication/logon events carry the real signal, rather than firewall or antivirus logs?
options: An attacker moving laterally typically authenticates to new hosts using harvested credentials, so that behavior shows up in authentication events
Lateral movement never generates any log data at all
Firewall logs always contain more detail than authentication logs
Antivirus logs are the only log source SIEMs can ingest
questions.explain: The behavior that defines lateral movement — authenticating to new hosts with harvested credentials — is visible in authentication logs.

questions.q: In the lateral-movement correlation logic, why group by user account and count distinct destination hosts, rather than just counting total authentication events?
options: Because distinct hosts and total events always produce identical counts
Because the real pattern is one account reaching an unusual number of distinct hosts quickly, not simply a high volume of logons overall
Because grouping by account is required by law for authentication logs
Because counting total events is technically impossible in a SIEM
questions.explain: Lateral movement looks like one account spreading to many hosts fast, which distinct-host counting captures and raw event counts do not.

questions.q: Why is simply enabling every out-of-the-box rule a SIEM ships with described as a real anti-pattern?
options: Generic pre-built rules are written for a generic environment, so many end up irrelevant to your log sources, noisy against your normal traffic, or silent on your organization's actual risks
SIEM vendors charge extra for every rule enabled
Pre-built rules are identical to custom use cases in every respect
Out-of-the-box rules are always disabled by default and cannot be turned on
questions.explain: A rule written for a generic environment rarely matches any one organization's actual log sources, traffic, or risks.

questions.q: How does use-case development connect back to the tuning process from Lesson 15?
options: The two processes are unrelated and never interact
Use-case development replaces tuning entirely, so tuned rules never need use cases
Tuning only applies to out-of-the-box rules, never to custom use cases
A use case's correlation logic still needs baseline-driven thresholds and ongoing tuning before its alerts are trustworthy
questions.explain: Even a well-designed, risk-driven use case still needs its thresholds tuned against the organization's real baseline.
